headline: IRCTC files Regulation 31(4) disclosure under SEBI Takeover Code
sum: IRCTC submitted a mandatory Regulation 31(4) disclosure to NSE, signalling a substantial acquisition threshold breach (5%+ shares) or change of control by an acquiring party. The filing triggers mandatory immediate public disclosure obligations under the SEBI Takeover Regulations 2011.
implication: Regulation 31(4) disclosures are gating events in Indian M&A: they signal imminent formal takeover announcements and may trigger open offer obligations if the acquirer's holding post-acquisition exceeds 25% without prior board/shareholder approval.
detail: IRCTC, the Government of India's listed railway hospitality and tourism operator, filed a formal disclosure under Regulation 31(4) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011. This regulation mandates that any person acquiring 5% or more shares, or any acquisition resulting in a change of control, must disclose the transaction to the stock exchange within two trading days. The filing was submitted to NSE on or around 19 June 2026.

framework.note: Mandatory disclosure requirement: person acquiring 5%+ shares or acquiring control must disclose within 2 trading days to stock exchange.
Definition of 'acquirer' and 'acquisition' triggering takeover code applicability.
Open offer triggers: 25% shareholding threshold or acquirer becoming largest shareholder.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, Section 23
framework.note: SEBI's regulatory authority over takeover regulation and disclosure enforcement.
Definition of 'public company' and applicability scope for IRCTC.
Exceptions and exemptions (e.g., government acquisitions or holding co. restructurings).

conditions: Acquirer shareholding equals or exceeds 5%, or acquirer acquires change of control
approvals: Stock Exchange (NSE) receipt and public disclosure
Potential: NCLT approval if scheme-based (not applicable if simple share purchase)

triggers.note: Mandatory 2-day disclosure post-acquisition; may trigger open offer under Regulation 5 (25% threshold)
If acquisition results in 25%+ holding, open offer may be triggered unless exemption applies
